categories.name: Prompt Injection Research
categories.summary: Heavy research focus on prompt injection attack vectors and defenses. Studies reveal that clarification-seeking behaviors in agents amplify injection vulnerability, while contextual manipulation can bypass traditional data/instruction separation. Practical tools for testing injection scenarios in controlled environments are emerging.

key_items.title: Clarification requests amplify prompt injection success rates
key_items.detail: ASPI research shows prompt injection succeeds more often when agents solicit clarification from users, suggesting clarification channels need distinct trust boundary treatment.

key_items.title: Contextual Integrity as evaluation lens for injection attacks
key_items.detail: New paper argues traditional data/instruction separation fails against contextual manipulation, proposing CI-aware alignment to detect context-sensitive agent failures.

key_items.title: IPI-proxy for red-teaming web-browsing agents
key_items.detail: Intercepting proxy enables testing indirect prompt injection on live retrieval paths by injecting payloads into whitelisted HTTP responses.

key_items.title: PromptForage hands-on injection lab released
key_items.detail: Interactive lab environment for reproducing and documenting prompt injection patterns before deploying tool or data-access privileges.

categories.name: Agent Security & Credential Management
categories.summary: Significant attention on securing AI agent credential flows and supply chains. Credential brokering emerges as a key pattern to limit blast radius, while supply-chain attacks via 'payload-less skills' highlight gaps in static analysis. Major password manager adds scoped token sharing for agents.

key_items.title: Credential brokering reduces prompt injection blast radius
key_items.detail: Pattern keeps long-lived secrets out of model context, brokering short-lived policy-scoped access at tool boundaries with authZ enforced outside the agent.

key_items.title: Payload-less skills exploit agent supply chains
key_items.detail: Research shows benign-looking skills can steer agents via natural-language compliance rules, bypassing signature and code scanners entirely.

key_items.title: Proton Pass adds scoped AI agent credential sharing
key_items.detail: New feature provides monitored, scoped tokens for vault items with activity visibility, though enforcement must occur at token layer not UX.

categories.name: Vulnerabilities & CVEs
categories.summary: Two notable CVEs affecting AI tooling disclosed. PydanticAI's SSRF blocklist can be bypassed via IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses, and Kiro CLI allows unauthorized tool execution through piped stdin. Both highlight the brittleness of blocklist-only and input-source validation approaches.

key_items.title: CVE-2026-46678: PydanticAI SSRF blocklist bypass
key_items.detail: Cloud-metadata IP blocklist bypassed using IPv6 transition form encoding; network-boundary egress validation recommended over blocklist-only defenses.

key_items.title: CVE-2026-9255: Kiro CLI stdin authorization bypass
key_items.detail: Missing input-source validation allows piped stdin to be treated as trusted, enabling shell execution without user approval.

categories.name: AI-Assisted Vulnerability Discovery
categories.summary: Anthropic's Project Glasswing update reveals Claude Mythos Preview has identified over 10,000 high/critical vulnerabilities in essential software within one month. This accelerates pressure on developers to shorten patch cycles as AI-powered vulnerability discovery scales.

key_items.title: Claude Mythos discovers 10,000+ critical vulnerabilities
key_items.detail: Anthropic's unreleased frontier model has uncovered massive vulnerability counts, prompting advice to shorten patch cycles across the industry.

key_items.title: Glasswing initial research update published
key_items.detail: Anthropic releases details on their AI-assisted security research initiative and early findings.

key_items.title: CERT.PL on autonomous fuzzing
key_items.detail: Technical post exploring autonomous fuzzing techniques for vulnerability discovery.

top_insights: Prompt injection attack surface is expanding beyond execution-time tool returns to include clarification flows and contextual manipulation, requiring trust boundary reevaluation.
AI agent credential security is maturing toward brokered, short-lived, policy-scoped access patterns rather than passing credentials through model context.
Supply-chain attacks on AI agents can leverage natural-language 'compliance rules' in skills that evade traditional static analysis—intent-based evaluation is essential.
AI-assisted vulnerability discovery is scaling dramatically; Anthropic's 10,000+ findings in one month signals a potential shift in attacker-defender dynamics requiring faster patch cycles.
Multiple CVEs show that blocklist-only and input-source validation approaches remain brittle; defense-in-depth at network and architectural layers is critical.
